source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Aramaic. **THE NIGHT VISION** — the most cross-corpus-dense single chapter in the Hebrew Bible after Gen 1 and Isa 53. SECONDARY: 4Q112 (Daniela) preserves substantial fragments of ch 7; 4Q113 (Danielb) preserves portions. The Qumran witnesses confirm the MT outline; minor orthographic variants only. TERTIARY: OG-Greek + Theodotion-Greek diverge at several text-critical points, most notably at v 13 (the 'son of man'-formula has different prepositions: Aramaic *ʿim ʿănānê šəmayyāʾ* 'with the clouds of heaven' vs OG *epi tōn nephelōn* 'upon the clouds' vs Th *meta tōn nephelōn* 'with the clouds'). Theodotion is closer to MT.
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against BHS apparatus + DJD XVI 2000 + Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.fetchedFrom: BHS; Ulrich DJD XVI 2000; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999; 1 En 14 throne-vision per Nickelsburg 2001.
source.citation: BHS (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich et al. 2000 DJD XVI; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 7 — ARAMAIC, the four beasts + the Ancient of Days + the Son of Man + the kingdom of the holy ones. This is the LAST chapter in Aramaic; ch 8 returns to Hebrew. The chapter is the structural climax of the chiastic Aramaic core (chs 2-7), pairing with ch 2 (the four kingdoms reappear in bestial-symbolic form). **CROSS-CORPUS DENSITY**: every verse from 7:9-14 is cited or alluded to in: (a) 1 En 14, 46-48, 60-71 (the Similitudes of Enoch + Book of the Watchers throne-vision); (b) 4 Ezra 13 (the man-from-the-sea vision); (c) NT — Mark 13:26, 14:62; Matt 24:30, 26:64, 28:18; Luke 21:27, 22:69; John 5:27; Acts 7:55-56; Rev 1:7, 1:13-15, 4-5, 11:15, 14:14, 20:11-12. The Son-of-Man formula is THE most contested Christological text in scripture.

verses.text: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת חֲדָ֗ה לְבֵלְאשַׁצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל דָּנִיֵּאל֙ חֵ֣לֶם חֲזָ֔ה וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשֵׁ֖הּ עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבֵ֑הּ בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ חֶלְמָ֣א כְתַ֔ב רֵ֥אשׁ מִלִּ֖ין אֲמַֽר׃
verses.translit: bi-šnaṯ ḥăḏāh lə-Bēlšaʾṣṣar meleḵ Bāḇel Dāniyyēʾl ḥēlem ḥăzāh wə-ḥezwê rēšēh ʿal-miškəḇēh bēʾḏayin ḥelmāʾ ḵəṯaḇ rēʾš millîn ʾămar
verses.notes: **In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream and visions of his head as he lay in his bed; then he wrote down the dream, and told the sum of the matter.** **CHRONOLOGICAL FRAMING**: the vision is dated to Belshazzar's first year — chronologically BEFORE the ch 5 feast and Belshazzar's death (which falls in his last year). The narrative chronology of the book is non-linear. Belshazzar's regency began c. 553 BCE (when Nabonidus departed for Teima), giving a notional date for this vision.

verses.text: עָנֵ֤ה דָנִיֵּאל֙ וְאָמַ֔ר חָזֵ֥ה הֲוֵ֛ית בְּחֶזְוִ֖י עִם־לֵֽילְיָ֑א וַאֲר֗וּ אַרְבַּע֙ רוּחֵ֣י שְׁמַיָּ֔א מְגִיחָ֖ן לְיַמָּ֥א רַבָּֽא׃
verses.translit: ʿănēh Dāniyyēʾl wə-ʾāmar ḥāzēh hăwêṯ bə-ḥezwî ʿim-lêləyāʾ wa-ʾărū ʾarbaʿ rūḥê šəmayyāʾ məḡîḥān lə-yammāʾ rabbāʾ
verses.notes: **Daniel said: 'I saw in my vision by night, and behold, the four winds of heaven were stirring up the great sea.'** **THE FOUR WINDS + THE GREAT SEA**: cosmogonic imagery — the *Chaoskampf* (combat with the chaotic sea) from Gen 1:2; Ps 74:12-17; Job 26:12-13; Isa 27:1. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 7:1 (four winds + four corners of the earth); cf. Zech 6:1-5 (four chariots = four winds). The sea is the source of the beasts that follow.

verses.text: וְאַרְבַּ֤ע חֵיוָן֙ רַבְרְבָ֔ן סָלְקָ֖ן מִן־יַמָּ֑א שָׁנְיָ֖ן דָּ֥א מִן־דָּֽא׃
verses.translit: wə-ʾarbaʿ ḥêwān raḇrəḇān sāləqān min-yammāʾ šānyān dāʾ min-dāʾ
verses.notes: **And four great beasts came up out of the sea, different from one another.** **THE FOUR BEASTS = FOUR KINGDOMS** — parallel to the four-metal statue of ch 2. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: cf. Rev 13:1 ('a beast rising out of the sea... with ten horns and seven heads') — Revelation conflates Daniel's four distinct beasts into one composite beast. cf. 4 Ezra 11-12 (the eagle from the sea), which explicitly cites Dan 7 (4 Ezra 12:11).

verses.text: קַדְמָיְתָ֣א כְאַרְיֵ֔ה וְגַפִּ֥ין דִּֽי־נְשַׁ֖ר לַ֑הּ חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֡ית עַד֩ דִּי־מְרִ֨יטוּ גַפַּ֜יהּ וּנְטִ֣ילַת מִן־אַרְעָ֗א וְעַל־רַגְלַ֙יִן֙ כֶּאֱנָ֣שׁ הֳקִימַ֔ת וּלְבַ֥ב אֱנָ֖שׁ יְהִ֥יב לַֽהּ׃
verses.translit: qaḏmāyəṯāʾ ḵə-ʾaryēh wə-gappîn dî-nəšar lah ḥāzēh hăwêṯ ʿaḏ dî-mərîṭū ḡappayh ū-nəṭîlaṯ min-ʾarʿāʾ wə-ʿal-raḡlayin ke-ʾĕnāš hŏqîmaṯ ū-ləḇaḇ ʾĕnāš yəhîḇ lah
verses.notes: **The first was like a lion, and had eagle's wings. As I looked, its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the ground and made to stand upon two feet like a man; and the mind of a man was given to it.** **FIRST BEAST = BABYLON** (per traditional four-kingdoms reading: Babylon-Media-Persia-Greece, or Babylon-Persia-Greece-Rome per Christian/Josephus tradition). **ICONOGRAPHY**: the winged-lion is the standard Babylonian symbol — attested on Ishtar Gate friezes (the *mušḫuššu* dragon-creature). The mind-of-a-man transformation echoes Nebuchadnezzar's restoration in 4:34. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 13:2 (Revelation's composite beast 'like a leopard, its feet like a bear, its mouth like a lion's' — assembles Daniel's beasts into one).

verses.text: וַאֲר֣וּ חֵיוָה֩ אָחֳרִ֨י תִנְיָנָ֜ה דָּמְיָ֣ה לְדֹ֗ב וְלִשְׂטַר־חַד֙ הֳקִמַ֔ת וּתְלָ֥ת עִלְעִ֛ין בְּפֻמַּ֖הּ בֵּ֣ין שניה שִׁנַּ֑יהּ וְכֵן֙ אָמְרִ֣ין לַ֔הּ ק֥וּמִֽי אֲכֻ֖לִי בְּשַׂ֥ר שַׂגִּֽיא׃
verses.translit: wa-ʾărū ḥêwāh ʾoḥŏrî ṯinyānāh dāməyāh lə-ḏōḇ wə-li-śṭar-ḥaḏ hŏqimaṯ ū-ṯəlāṯ ʿilʿîn bə-p̄ummah bên šinnayh wə-ḵēn ʾāmərîn lah qūmî ʾăḵulî bəśar śaggîʾ
verses.notes: **And behold, another beast, a second one, like a bear; it was raised up on one side; it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth; and it was told: Arise, devour much flesh.** **SECOND BEAST = MEDIA** (traditional) or **MEDO-PERSIA** (per Christian/Rev 13 reading). The three ribs may symbolize three conquered kingdoms (per Goldingay 1989: Babylon, Lydia, Egypt under Cyrus/Cambyses). Qere-ketiv: שניה/שִׁנַּיה.

verses.text: בָּאתַ֨ר דְּנָ֜ה חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֗ית וַאֲר֤וּ אָֽחֳרִי֙ כִּנְמַ֔ר וְלַ֨הּ גַּפִּ֥ין אַרְבַּ֛ע דִּי־ע֖וֹף עַל־גביה גַּבַּ֑יהּ וְאַרְבְּעָ֤ה רֵאשִׁין֙ לְחֵ֣יוְתָ֔א וְשָׁלְטָ֖ן יְהִ֥יב לַֽהּ׃
verses.translit: bāʾṯar dənāh ḥāzēh hăwêṯ wa-ʾărū ʾoḥŏrî ki-nmar wə-lah gappîn ʾarbaʿ dî-ʿōp̄ ʿal-gabbayh wə-ʾarbəʿāh rēšîn lə-ḥêwəṯāʾ wə-šolṭān yəhîḇ lah
verses.notes: **After this I looked, and behold, another, like a leopard, with four wings of a bird on its back; and the beast had four heads; and dominion was given to it.** **THIRD BEAST = PERSIA** (traditional) or **GREECE** (per Christian/Antiochene reading). The four heads = four successor-kingdoms of Alexander (per Collins 1993: Ptolemies, Seleucids, Antigonids, Attalids/Cassander's Macedonia). Qere-ketiv: גביה/גַּבַּיה.

verses.text: בָּאתַ֣ר דְּנָה֩ חָזֵ֨ה הֲוֵ֜ית בְּחֶזְוֵ֣י לֵֽילְיָ֗א וַאֲר֣וּ ׀ חֵיוָ֣ה רביעיה רְֽבִיעָאָ֡ה דְּחִילָה֩ וְאֵֽימְתָנִ֨י וְתַקִּיפָ֜א יַתִּ֗ירָה וְשִׁנַּ֤יִן דִּֽי־פַרְזֶל֙ לַ֣הּ רַבְרְבָ֔ן אָֽכְלָ֣ה וּמַדֱּקָ֔ה וּשְׁאָרָ֖א ברגליה בְּרַגְלַ֣הּ רָפְסָ֑ה וְהִ֣יא מְשַׁנְּיָ֗ה מִן־כָּל־חֵֽיוָתָא֙ דִּ֣י קָֽדָמַ֔יהּ וְקַרְנַ֥יִן עֲשַׂ֖ר לַֽהּ׃
verses.translit: bāʾṯar dənāh ḥāzēh hăwêṯ bə-ḥezwê lêləyāʾ wa-ʾărū ḥêwāh rəḇîʿāʾāh dəḥîlāh wə-ʾêməṯānî wə-ṯaqqîpāʾ yattîrāh wə-šinnayin dî-p̄arzel lah raḇrəḇān ʾāḵəlāh ū-maddĕqāh ū-šəʾārāʾ bə-raḡlah rāp̄əsāh wə-hîʾ məšannəyāh min-kol-ḥêwāṯāʾ dī qodāmayh wə-qarnayin ʿăśar lah
verses.notes: **After this I saw in the night visions, and behold, a fourth beast, terrible and dreadful and exceedingly strong; it had great iron teeth, and devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet; it was different from all the beasts that were before it, and it had ten horns.** **FOURTH BEAST = GREECE/SELEUCIDS** (per Collins 1993 + scholarly consensus) or **ROME** (per Christian/Josephus/Rev 13 reading). The IRON-teeth correlate to the iron-legs of the ch 2 statue. **TEN HORNS**: per the Maccabean reading, the ten Seleucid kings from Seleucus I to Antiochus IV. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: cf. Rev 13:1 ('ten horns and seven heads'); Rev 17:3, 17:7, 17:12, 17:16 (the ten horns = ten kings). Revelation's beast-iconography is direct Dan 7:7 inheritance. Qere-ketiv: רביעיה/רְבִיעָאָה; ברגליה/בְּרַגְלַהּ.

verses.text: מִשְׂתַּכַּ֨ל הֲוֵ֜ית בְּקַרְנַיָּ֗א וַ֠אֲלוּ קֶ֣רֶן אָחֳרִ֤י זְעֵירָה֙ סִלְקָ֣ת ביניהון בֵּֽינֵיהֵ֔ן וּתְלָ֗ת מִן־קַרְנַיָּא֙ קַדְמָ֣יָתָ֔א אתעקרו אֶתְעֲקַ֖רָה מִן־קדמיה קֳדָמַ֑הּ וַאֲל֨וּ עַיְנִ֜ין כְּעַיְנֵ֤י אֲנָשָׁא֙ בְּקַרְנָא־דָ֔א וּפֻ֖ם מְמַלִּ֥ל רַבְרְבָֽן׃
verses.translit: miśtakkal hăwêṯ bə-qarnayyāʾ wa-ʾălū qeren ʾoḥŏrî zəʿêrāh siləqāṯ bênêhēn ū-ṯəlāṯ min-qarnayyāʾ qaḏmāyāṯāʾ ʾeṯʿăqarāh min-qodāmah wa-ʾălū ʿaynîn kə-ʿaynê ʾănāšāʾ bə-qarnāʾ-ḏāʾ ū-p̄um məmallil raḇrəḇān
verses.notes: **I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots; and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.** **THE LITTLE HORN = ANTIOCHUS IV EPIPHANES** (per the dominant scholarly consensus: Collins 1993, Newsom 2014, Hartman-DiLella 1978). The three uprooted horns = three Seleucid rivals Antiochus IV eliminated (Heliodorus, Seleucus IV's son Demetrius I, and Ptolemaic candidate Antiochus). **'MOUTH SPEAKING GREAT THINGS'** (פֻם מְמַלִּל רַבְרְבָן pum məmallil raḇrəḇān): the blasphemy-motif. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: cf. Rev 13:5-6 ('the beast was given a mouth uttering haughty and blasphemous words... it opened its mouth to utter blasphemies against God'); cf. 2 Thess 2:3-4 (the man of lawlessness exalting himself). Qere-ketiv: ביניהון/בֵּינֵיהֵן; אתעקרו/אֶתְעֲקַרָה; קדמיה/קֳדָמַהּ.

verses.text: חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֗ית עַ֣ד דִּ֤י כָרְסָוָן֙ רְמִ֔יו וְעַתִּ֥יק יוֹמִ֖ין יְתִ֑ב לְבוּשֵׁ֣הּ ׀ כִּתְלַ֣ג חִוָּ֗ר וּשְׂעַ֤ר רֵאשֵׁהּ֙ כַּעֲמַ֣ר נְקֵ֔א כָּרְסְיֵהּ֙ שְׁבִיבִ֣ין דִּי־נ֔וּר גַּלְגִּלּ֖וֹהִי נ֥וּר דָּלִֽק׃
verses.translit: ḥāzēh hăwêṯ ʿaḏ dī ḵorsāwān rəmîw wə-ʿattîq yōmîn yəṯiḇ ləḇūšēh ki-ṯlaḡ ḥiwwār ū-śəʿar rēšēh ka-ʿămar nəqēʾ korsəyēh šəḇîḇîn dî-nūr galgillōhî nūr dāliq
verses.notes: **As I looked, thrones were placed and one that was Ancient of Days took his seat; his raiment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, its wheels were burning fire.** **THE ANCIENT OF DAYS — ʿATTĪQ YŌMĪN — MAJOR CROSS-CORPUS NODE**: עַתִּיק יוֹמִין (ʿattîq yōmîn) — appears only here, v 13, v 22 in HB. **CROSS-CORPUS — FOUNDATIONAL**: (a) 1 En 14:18-22 (the Book of the Watchers throne-vision: 'a lofty throne — its appearance was like crystal, and its wheels like the shining sun... the Great Glory sat on it, and his raiment was brighter than the sun and whiter than any snow') — 1 En 14 is the closest extant parallel and is widely held to predate Daniel; the two visions share a common throne-vision tradition. (b) Ezek 1:26-28 + Isa 6 — earlier throne-visions. (c) Rev 1:13-15 (Christ's hair 'white as wool, white as snow'; 'eyes like a flame of fire'; 'feet like burnished bronze') — Revelation 1:13-15 transfers the Ancient of Days iconography ONTO the risen Christ, fusing Dan 7:9 (the Ancient) with Dan 7:13 (the Son of Man). This is the foundational Christological move. (d) Rev 20:11-12 ('a great white throne... books were opened'). (e) Jub heavenly tablets tradition. The 'thrones' (plural — כָרְסָוָן korsāwān) raise the question of the second-throne; b. Hagigah 14a's debate (Akiba: 'one for him, one for David'; the Sages: 'one for justice, one for righteousness'); the Christian reading: one for the Ancient, one for the Son of Man (v 13).

verses.text: נְהַ֣ר דִּי־נ֗וּר נָגֵ֤ד וְנָפֵק֙ מִן־קֳדָמ֔וֹהִי אֶ֤לֶף אלפים אַלְפִין֙ יְשַׁמְּשׁוּנֵּ֔הּ וְרִבּ֥וֹ רבון רִבְבָ֖ן קָֽדָמ֣וֹהִי יְקוּמ֑וּן דִּינָ֥א יְתִ֖ב וְסִפְרִ֥ין פְּתִֽיחוּ׃
verses.translit: nəhar dî-nūr nāḡēḏ wə-nāp̄ēq min-qodāmōhî ʾelep̄ ʾalpîn yəšamməšūnnēh wə-ribbō riḇḇān qodāmōhî yəqūmūn dînāʾ yəṯiḇ wə-sip̄rîn pəṯîḥū
verses.notes: **A stream of fire issued and came forth from before him; a thousand thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him; the court sat in judgment, and the books were opened.** **MAJOR APOCALYPTIC NODE**: (a) **RIVER OF FIRE**: cf. 1 En 14:19 ('streams of flaming fire issued forth from beneath the throne'); (b) **THOUSAND THOUSANDS + TEN THOUSAND TIMES TEN THOUSAND**: the angelic host. cf. Deut 33:2 ('he came from the ten thousands of holy ones'); cf. Ps 68:17 ('the chariots of God are twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands'); cf. 1 En 40:1, 60:1, 71:8 (the myriad-myriads of angels); (c) **BOOKS OPENED**: the heavenly judgment-books. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: cf. Rev 5:11 ('I heard the voice of many angels... numbering myriads of myriads, and thousands of thousands') — DIRECT Dan 7:10 quotation; cf. Rev 20:12 ('the books were opened... and another book was opened, which is the book of life; and the dead were judged from what was written in the books, according to what they had done') — Rev 20:12 cites Dan 7:10 verbatim. cf. Jub 30:22 (heavenly tablets); 1 En 47:3 (books opened at judgment); 1 En 90:20. The Daniel 7:10 verse is THE foundational scripture for the final-judgment-books tradition. Qere-ketiv: אלפים/אַלְפִין; רבון/רִבְבָן.

verses.text: חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית בֵּאדַ֗יִן מִן־קָל֙ מִלַּיָּ֣א רַבְרְבָתָ֔א דִּ֥י קַרְנָ֖א מְמַלֱּלָ֑ה חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֡ית עַד֩ דִּ֨י קְטִילַ֤ת חֵֽיוְתָא֙ וְהוּבַ֣ד גִּשְׁמַ֔הּ וִיהִיבַ֖ת לִיקֵדַ֥ת אֶשָּֽׁא׃
verses.translit: ḥāzēh hăwêṯ bēʾḏayin min-qāl millayyāʾ raḇrəḇāṯāʾ dī qarnāʾ məmallĕlāh ḥāzēh hăwêṯ ʿaḏ dī qəṭîlaṯ ḥêwəṯāʾ wə-hūḇaḏ gišmah wî-hîḇaṯ lî-qêḏaṯ ʾeššāʾ
verses.notes: **I looked then because of the sound of the great words which the horn was speaking. And as I looked, the beast was slain, and its body destroyed and given over to be burned with fire.** **THE BEAST'S DESTRUCTION**: judgment executed against the fourth-beast/little-horn. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 19:20 ('the beast was captured... thrown alive into the lake of fire'). cf. Rev 20:10 ('the devil... was thrown into the lake of fire').

verses.text: וּשְׁאָר֙ חֵֽיוָתָ֔א הֶעְדִּ֖יו שָׁלְטָנְה֑וֹן וְאַרְכָ֧ה בְחַיִּ֛ין יְהִ֥יבַת לְה֖וֹן עַד־זְמַ֥ן וְעִדָּֽן׃
verses.translit: ū-šəʾār ḥêwāṯāʾ heʿdîw šolṭānə-hōn wə-ʾarḵāh ḇə-ḥayyîn yəhîḇaṯ lə-hōn ʿaḏ-zəman wə-ʿiddān
verses.notes: **As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away, but their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.** The first three beasts survive in subordinated form, the fourth is destroyed. **TERM**: זְמַן וְעִדָּן (zəman wə-ʿiddān 'season and time') — the chronological apocalyptic vocabulary.

verses.text: חָזֵ֤ה הֲוֵית֙ בְּחֶזְוֵ֣י לֵֽילְיָ֔א וַאֲרוּ֙ עִם־עֲנָנֵ֣י שְׁמַיָּ֔א כְּבַ֥ר אֱנָ֖שׁ אָתֵ֣ה הֲוָ֑ה וְעַד־עַתִּ֤יק יֽוֹמַיָּא֙ מְטָ֔ה וּקְדָמ֖וֹהִי הַקְרְבֽוּהִי׃
verses.translit: ḥāzēh hăwêṯ bə-ḥezwê lêləyāʾ wa-ʾărū ʿim-ʿănānê šəmayyāʾ kə-ḇar ʾĕnāš ʾāṯēh hăwāh wə-ʿaḏ-ʿattîq yōmayyāʾ məṭāh ū-qədāmōhî haqrəḇūhî
verses.witness_tertiary: OG-Greek: ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὡς υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἤρχετο 'upon the clouds of heaven as a son of man was coming'; Theodotion: μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὡς υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενος ἦν 'with the clouds of heaven as a son of man was coming'. The MT עִם 'with' corresponds more closely to Theodotion (μετά) than OG (ἐπί).
verses.notes: **I saw in the night visions, and behold, with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man, and he came to the Ancient of Days and was presented before him.** **THE SON OF MAN — KEBAR ʾĔNĀŠ — THE MOST CONTESTED VERSE IN THE HB**. **KEY ARAMAIC**: כְּבַר אֱנָשׁ (kə-ḇar ʾĕnāš 'like a son of man' / 'one like a human one'). **THE CRUX**: is the figure (a) corporate symbol = the holy ones of the Most High (v 27); (b) angelic = Michael (per Collins 1993, Newsom 2014, who note vv 21-22, 25-27 identify the human-figure with the persecuted saints); (c) divine pre-existent Messiah (per 1 En 46-48 'son of man' / Similitudes; 4 Ezra 13; later Christian tradition); (d) the human-historical Jesus (per Mark 14:62 + Matt 26:64). **CROSS-CORPUS — THE NT QUOTATIONS**: (i) **Mark 14:62 + Matt 26:64 + Luke 22:69**: at his trial Jesus combines Dan 7:13 (Son of Man + clouds) with Ps 110:1 (right hand of power) — the single most explicit self-identification with Daniel's figure. (ii) **Mark 13:26 + Matt 24:30 + Luke 21:27**: the Olivet discourse — 'they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory' = Dan 7:13 verbatim. (iii) **Matt 28:18**: 'all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me' = Dan 7:14 conferral. (iv) **Rev 1:7**: 'Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him' — Dan 7:13 + Zech 12:10 conflated. (v) **Rev 1:13**: 'one like a son of man' (ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου) — exact Aramaic-Greek translation of kə-ḇar ʾĕnāš. (vi) **Rev 14:14**: 'a son of man, with a golden crown'. (vii) **Acts 7:55-56**: Stephen's vision — 'the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God'. (viii) **John 5:27**: 'authority to execute judgment because he is the Son of Man' — direct Dan 7:13-14 inheritance. **CROSS-CORPUS — 1 ENOCH SIMILITUDES (chs 37-71)**: the 'son of man' (par-/bar enash) is named 35 times, identified as 'the Chosen One', pre-existent (1 En 48:3, 48:6), enthroned (1 En 62), receives universal worship (1 En 62:6-9); 1 En 71 identifies the Son of Man with Enoch himself. The Similitudes (1st century BCE-CE) directly elaborate Dan 7:13. **CROSS-CORPUS — 4 EZRA 13**: the man-from-the-sea figure, explicitly cites Dan 7. **CROSS-CORPUS — RABBINIC**: b. Sanhedrin 98a (R. Yehoshua ben Levi: the Messiah comes 'with the clouds of heaven' if Israel is worthy, 'lowly riding upon an ass' (Zech 9:9) if not) — direct rabbinic exegesis of Dan 7:13.

verses.text: וְלֵ֨הּ יְהִ֤יב שָׁלְטָן֙ וִיקָ֣ר וּמַלְכ֔וּ וְכֹ֣ל עַֽמְמַיָּ֗א אֻמַיָּ֛א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֖א לֵ֣הּ יִפְלְח֑וּן שָׁלְטָנֵ֞הּ שָׁלְטָ֤ן עָלַם֙ דִּֽי־לָ֣א יֶעְדֵּ֔ה וּמַלְכוּתֵ֖הּ דִּי־לָ֥א תִתְחַבַּֽל׃
verses.translit: wə-lēh yəhîḇ šolṭān wî-qār ū-malḵū wə-ḵōl ʿammə-mayyāʾ ʾummayyāʾ wə-liššānayyāʾ lēh yip̄ləḥūn šolṭānēh šolṭān ʿālam dî-lāʾ yeʿdēh ū-malḵūṯēh dî-lāʾ ṯiṯḥabbal
verses.notes: **And to him was given dominion and glory and kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him; his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom one that shall not be destroyed.** **THE CONFERRAL OF UNIVERSAL DOMINION**: the eternal-kingdom refrain at its theological climax. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR NT**: (a) Matt 28:18 ('All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me') — the post-resurrection Great Commission directly inherits Dan 7:14. (b) Phil 2:9-11 ('God has highly exalted him... at the name of Jesus every knee should bow... and every tongue confess'). (c) Rev 11:15 ('The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign forever and ever'). (d) Rev 5:13 (universal worship). (e) Eph 1:20-22. The tripartite formula 'peoples, nations, languages' (Daniel-Aramaic distinctive) repeats.

verses.text: אֶתְכְּרִיַּ֥ת רוּחִ֛י אֲנָ֥ה דָנִיֵּ֖אל בְּג֣וֹא נִדְנֶ֑ה וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י יְבַהֲלֻנַּֽנִי׃
verses.translit: ʾeṯkəriyyaṯ rūḥî ʾănāh Dāniyyēʾl bə-ḡōʾ niḏneh wə-ḥezwê rēšî yəḇahălunnannî
verses.notes: **As for me, Daniel, my spirit within me was anxious, and the visions of my head alarmed me.** **TERM**: נִדְנֶה (niḏneh 'sheath') — metaphor for the body as scabbard for the spirit/soul; an interesting Aramaic anthropological idiom.

verses.text: קִרְבֵ֗ת עַל־חַד֙ מִן־קָ֣אֲמַיָּ֔א וְיַצִּיבָ֥א אֶבְעֵֽא־מִנֵּ֖הּ עַֽל־כָּל־דְּנָ֑ה וַאֲמַר־לִ֕י וּפְשַׁ֥ר מִלַּיָּ֖א יְהוֹדְעִנַּֽנִי׃
verses.translit: qirḇēṯ ʿal-ḥaḏ min-qāʾămayyāʾ wə-yaṣṣîḇāʾ ʾeḇʿēʾ-minnēh ʿal-kol-dənāh wa-ʾămar-lî ū-p̄əšar millayyāʾ yə-hōḏəʿinnannî
verses.notes: **I approached one of those who stood there and asked him the truth concerning all this. So he told me, and made known to me the interpretation of the things.** The *angelus interpres* (interpreting angel) motif — a stock feature of late apocalyptic. cf. Zech 1-6; 1 En 17-36; 4 Ezra; Rev.

verses.text: אִלֵּין֙ חֵיוָתָ֣א רַבְרְבָתָ֔א דִּ֥י אִנִּ֖ין אַרְבַּ֑ע אַרְבְּעָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְקוּמ֥וּן מִן־אַרְעָֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾillên ḥêwāṯāʾ raḇrəḇāṯāʾ dī ʾinnîn ʾarbaʿ ʾarbəʿāh malḵîn yəqūmūn min-ʾarʿāʾ
verses.notes: **'These four great beasts are four kings who shall arise out of the earth.'** **'KINGS'** (מַלְכִין malḵîn) — but v 23 has 'kingdom' (מַלְכוּ malḵū) for the fourth. The terms are interchangeable; king-as-kingdom-personification.

verses.text: וִֽיקַבְּלוּן֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔א קַדִּישֵׁ֖י עֶלְיוֹנִ֑ין וְיַחְסְנ֤וּן מַלְכוּתָא֙ עַֽד־עָ֣לְמָ֔א וְעַ֖ד עָלַ֥ם עָלְמַיָּֽא׃
verses.translit: wî-qabbəlūn malḵūṯāʾ qaddîšê ʿelyōnîn wə-yaḥsənūn malḵūṯāʾ ʿaḏ-ʿāləmāʾ wə-ʿaḏ ʿālam ʿāləmayyāʾ
verses.notes: **'But the holy ones of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, for ever and ever.'** **THE HOLY ONES OF THE MOST HIGH** — קַדִּישֵׁי עֶלְיוֹנִין (qaddîšê ʿelyōnîn). Note the unusual Aramaic *ʿelyōnîn* (Most-High in plural) — the plural form (lit. 'highest [ones]') has been read as: (a) plural-of-majesty; (b) divine-council/angelic-host (Collins 1993 prefers the angelic reading); (c) Aramaic stylistic plural. **THE CORPORATE READING**: the kingdom-conferral on the Son of Man (v 14) is here paralleled by conferral on 'the holy ones' — establishing that the Son of Man IS / represents the holy-ones. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Matt 19:28 ('you who have followed me will sit on twelve thrones'); cf. Rev 20:4 ('they came to life and reigned with Christ'); cf. 1 Cor 6:2 ('the saints will judge the world'); cf. Rev 22:5 ('they will reign forever and ever') — the saints-co-reign tradition directly inherits Dan 7:18, 27.

verses.text: אֱדַ֗יִן צְבִית֙ לְיַצָּבָ֔א עַל־חֵֽיוְתָא֙ רְבִיעָ֣יְתָ֔א דִּֽי־הֲוָ֥ת שָֽׁנְיָ֖ה מִן־כלהון כָּלְּהֵ֑ין דְּחִילָ֣ה יַתִּ֗ירָה שניה שִׁנַּ֤הּ דִּֽי־פַרְזֶל֙ וטפריה וְטִפְרַ֣הּ דִּֽי־נְחָ֔שׁ אָֽכְלָ֣ה מַדֱּקָ֔ה וּשְׁאָרָ֖א בְּרַגְלַ֥הּ רָֽפְסָֽה׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin ṣəḇîṯ lə-yaṣṣāḇāʾ ʿal-ḥêwəṯāʾ rəḇîʿāyəṯāʾ dî-hăwāṯ šānyāh min-kolləhên dəḥîlāh yattîrāh šinnah dî-p̄arzel wə-ṭiprah dî-nəḥāš ʾāḵəlāh maddĕqāh ū-šəʾārāʾ bə-raḡlah rāp̄əsāh
verses.notes: **'Then I desired to know the truth concerning the fourth beast, which was different from all the rest, exceedingly terrible, with its teeth of iron and claws of bronze, and which devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet.'** Qere-ketiv (multiple): כלהון/כָּלְּהֵין; שניה/שִׁנַּהּ; וטפריה/וְטִפְרַהּ.

verses.text: וְעַל־קַרְנַיָּ֤א עֲשַׂר֙ דִּ֣י בְרֵאשַׁ֔הּ וְאָחֳרִי֙ דִּ֣י סִלְקַ֔ת ונפלו וּנְפַ֥לָה מִן־קדמיה קֳדָמַ֖הּ תְּלָ֑ת וְקַרְנָ֨א דִכֵּ֜ן וְעַיְנִ֣ין לַ֗הּ וְפֻם֙ מְמַלִּ֣ל רַבְרְבָ֔ן וְחֶזְוַ֖הּ רַ֥ב מִן־חַבְרָתַֽהּ׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿal-qarnayyāʾ ʿăśar dī ḇə-rēšah wə-ʾoḥŏrî dī siləqaṯ ū-nəp̄alāh min-qodāmah təlāṯ wə-qarnāʾ ḏikkēn wə-ʿaynîn lah wə-p̄um məmallil raḇrəḇān wə-ḥezwah raḇ min-ḥaḇrāṯah
verses.notes: **'And concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn which came up and before which three of them fell, the horn which had eyes and a mouth that spoke great things, and which seemed greater than its fellows.'** Qere-ketiv: ונפלו/וּנְפַלָה; קדמיה/קֳדָמַהּ.

verses.text: חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית וְקַרְנָ֣א דִכֵּ֔ן עָבְדָ֥ה קְרָ֖ב עִם־קַדִּישִׁ֑ין וְיָכְלָ֖ה לְהֽוֹן׃
verses.translit: ḥāzēh hăwêṯ wə-qarnāʾ ḏikkēn ʿāḇəḏāh qərāḇ ʿim-qaddîšîn wə-yāḵəlāh lə-hōn
verses.notes: **'As I looked, this horn made war with the holy ones, and prevailed over them.'** **THE PERSECUTION-OF-THE-SAINTS NARRATIVE**: critical for the Maccabean reading — Antiochus IV's persecution of Torah-observant Jews (1 Macc 1; 2 Macc 6-7). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 13:7 ('it was allowed to make war on the saints and to conquer them') — direct Dan 7:21 quotation.

verses.text: עַ֣ד דִּֽי־אֲתָ֗ה עַתִּיק֙ יֽוֹמַיָּ֔א וְדִינָ֣א יְהִ֔ב לְקַדִּישֵׁ֖י עֶלְיוֹנִ֑ין וְזִמְנָ֣א מְטָ֔ה וּמַלְכוּתָ֖א הֶחֱסִ֥נוּ קַדִּישִֽׁין׃
verses.translit: ʿaḏ dî-ʾăṯāh ʿattîq yōmayyāʾ wə-ḏînāʾ yəhiḇ lə-qaddîšê ʿelyōnîn wə-zimnāʾ məṭāh ū-malḵūṯāʾ heḥĕsinū qaddîšîn
verses.notes: **'Until the Ancient of Days came and judgment was given for the holy ones of the Most High, and the time came when the holy ones received the kingdom.'** **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. 1 Cor 6:2 ('the saints will judge the world'); cf. Rev 20:4. The 'judgment given FOR the holy ones' (לְקַדִּישֵׁי lə-qaddîšê — dative of advantage) is the vindication-verdict.

verses.text: כֵּן֮ אֲמַר֒ חֵֽיוְתָא֙ רְבִיעָ֣יְתָ֔א מַלְכ֤וּ רביעיא רְבִיעָאָה֙ תֶּהֱוֵ֣א בְאַרְעָ֔א דִּ֥י תִשְׁנֵ֖א מִן־כָּל־מַלְכְוָתָ֑א וְתֵאכֻל֙ כָּל־אַרְעָ֔א וּתְדוּשִׁנַּ֖הּ וְתַדְּקִנַּֽהּ׃
verses.translit: kēn ʾămar ḥêwəṯāʾ rəḇîʿāyəṯāʾ malḵū rəḇîʿāʾāh tehĕwēʾ ḇə-ʾarʿāʾ dī ṯišnēʾ min-kol-malḵəwāṯāʾ wə-ṯêḵul kol-ʾarʿāʾ ū-ṯəḏūšinnah wə-ṯaddəqinnah
verses.notes: **Thus he said: 'As for the fourth beast, there shall be a fourth kingdom on earth, which shall be different from all the kingdoms, and it shall devour the whole earth, and trample it down, and break it to pieces.'** Qere-ketiv: רביעיא/רְבִיעָאָה.

verses.text: וְקַרְנַיָּ֣א עֲשַׂ֔ר מִנַּהּ֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ה עַשְׂרָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְקֻמ֑וּן וְאָחֳרָ֞ן יְק֣וּם אַחֲרֵיה֗וֹן וְה֤וּא יִשְׁנֵא֙ מִן־קַדְמָיֵ֔א וּתְלָתָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְהַשְׁפִּֽל׃
verses.translit: wə-qarnayyāʾ ʿăśar minnah malḵūṯāh ʿaśrāh malḵîn yəqumūn wə-ʾoḥŏrān yəqūm ʾaḥărêhōn wə-hūʾ yišnēʾ min-qaḏmāyēʾ ū-ṯəlāṯāh malḵîn yəhašpil
verses.notes: **'As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings shall arise; and another shall arise after them; he shall be different from the former ones, and shall put down three kings.'** **MACCABEAN READING**: the ten kings = the Seleucid kings before Antiochus IV; 'another' = Antiochus IV; the three he 'put down' = his rivals. Numerical scheme is debated; per Collins 1993 the count includes Seleucus I + descendants.

verses.text: וּמִלִּ֗ין לְצַ֤ד עליא עִלָּאָה֙ יְמַלִּ֔ל וּלְקַדִּישֵׁ֥י עֶלְיוֹנִ֖ין יְבַלֵּ֑א וְיִסְבַּ֗ר לְהַשְׁנָיָה֙ זִמְנִ֣ין וְדָ֔ת וְיִתְיַהֲב֣וּן בִּידֵ֔הּ עַד־עִדָּ֥ן וְעִדָּנִ֖ין וּפְלַ֥ג עִדָּֽן׃
verses.translit: ū-millîn lə-ṣaḏ ʿillāʾāh yəmallil ū-lə-qaddîšê ʿelyōnîn yəḇallēʾ wə-yisbar lə-hašnāyāh zimnîn wə-ḏāṯ wə-yiṯyahăḇūn bî-ḏēh ʿaḏ-ʿiddān wə-ʿiddānîn ū-p̄əlaḡ ʿiddān
verses.notes: **'He shall speak words against the Most High, and shall wear out the holy ones of the Most High, and shall think to change the times and the law; and they shall be given into his hand for a time, two times, and half a time.'** **THE TIME-TIMES-HALF-A-TIME FORMULA** — עִדָּן וְעִדָּנִין וּפְלַג עִדָּן (ʿiddān wə-ʿiddānîn ū-p̄əlaḡ ʿiddān). **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: appears verbatim in Dan 12:7 (Hebrew מוֹעֵד מוֹעֲדִים וָחֵצִי môʿēḏ môʿăḏîm wā-ḥēṣî); and as 'forty-two months' / '1260 days' / 'time, times, and half a time' in Rev 11:2, 11:3, 12:6, 12:14, 13:5. The figure (3.5 years) corresponds to the duration of Antiochus IV's persecution / desecration of the Temple (167-164 BCE; precisely 3 years per 1 Macc 1:54 + 4:52, but the Daniel apocalyptic figure rounds to 3.5). **CHANGE THE TIMES AND THE LAW**: Antiochus IV altered the Jewish festival-calendar and proscribed Torah-observance per 1 Macc 1:41-50; this verse is the apocalyptic-interpretive lens. Qere-ketiv: עליא/עִלָּאָה.

verses.text: וְדִינָ֖א יִתִּ֑ב וְשָׁלְטָנֵ֣הּ יְהַעְדּ֔וֹן לְהַשְׁמָדָ֥ה וּלְהוֹבָדָ֖ה עַד־סוֹפָֽא׃
verses.translit: wə-ḏînāʾ yittiḇ wə-šolṭānēh yəhaʿdōn lə-hašmāḏāh ū-lə-hōḇāḏāh ʿaḏ-sōp̄āʾ
verses.notes: **'But the court shall sit in judgment, and his dominion shall be taken away, to be consumed and destroyed to the end.'**

verses.text: וּמַלְכוּתָ֨ה וְשָׁלְטָנָ֜א וּרְבוּתָ֗א דִּ֚י מַלְכְוָת֙ תְּח֣וֹת כָּל־שְׁמַיָּ֔א יְהִיבַ֕ת לְעַ֖ם קַדִּישֵׁ֣י עֶלְיוֹנִ֑ין מַלְכוּתֵהּ֙ מַלְכ֣וּת עָלַ֔ם וְכֹל֙ שָׁלְטָ֣נַיָּ֔א לֵ֥הּ יִפְלְח֖וּן וְיִֽשְׁתַּמְּעֽוּן׃
verses.translit: ū-malḵūṯāh wə-šolṭānāʾ ū-rəḇūṯāʾ dī malḵəwāṯ təḥōṯ kol-šəmayyāʾ yəhîḇaṯ lə-ʿam qaddîšê ʿelyōnîn malḵūṯēh malḵūṯ ʿālam wə-ḵōl šolṭānayyāʾ lēh yip̄ləḥūn wə-yištamməʿūn
verses.notes: **'And the kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High; their kingdom shall be an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey them.'** **THE FINAL EVERLASTING-KINGDOM REFRAIN** (cf. 2:44, 4:3, 4:34, 6:26, 7:14). **CRUCIAL TEXTUAL DETAIL**: the kingdom is given to 'the PEOPLE OF the saints' (עַם קַדִּישֵׁי ʿam qaddîšê) — the human-Israel readings; or to the angelic-saints with Israel as their people (Collins). The Aramaic is grammatically genuinely ambiguous.

verses.text: עַד־כָּ֖ה סוֹפָ֣א דִֽי־מִלְּתָ֑א אֲנָ֨ה דָֽנִיֵּ֜אל שַׂגִּ֣יא ׀ רַעְיוֹנַ֣י יְבַהֲלֻנַּ֗נִי וְזִיוַי֙ יִשְׁתַּנּ֣וֹן עֲלַ֔י וּמִלְּתָ֖א בְּלִבִּ֥י נִטְרֵֽת׃
verses.translit: ʿaḏ-kāh sōp̄āʾ ḏî-milləṯāʾ ʾănāh Dāniyyēʾl śaggîʾ raʿyōnay yəḇahălunnannî wə-zîway yištannōn ʿălay ū-milləṯāʾ bə-libbî niṭrēṯ
verses.notes: **Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly alarmed me, and my color changed; but I kept the matter in my mind.** **END OF ARAMAIC DANIEL** — the final word in Aramaic is נִטְרֵת ('I kept'). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Luke 2:19, 2:51 (Mary 'kept all these things, pondering them in her heart') — Lucan inheritance of the Danielic seer-formula. The next chapter returns to Hebrew.
